text:
maria: Customer says they got a 401 on /v1/generate and there's no Request ID in the response headers. They attached a screenshot and a wall-clock time (2026-03-16T14:08:19Z). Asked what to collect next.

devon: Ask them for a minimal curl repro (headers + body), a HAR export from the browser if it originated from web, or the SDK logs if from mobile/server. Also ask for the exact region they hit and the timestamp (they gave it, good).

maria: Quick steps I usually paste to customers: 1) Console -> Requests -> filter by timestamp -> click the row -> copy the "request_ref" value (it shows as Request ID). If they used SDK, tell them to look for `request_ref` in SDK logs or enable DEBUG to surface it.

maria: If they can't find it, ask them to export a debug bundle from Console (Settings -> Support -> Export debug token) and attach it here. The debug token lets us correlate on our side without sharing keys.

devon: HAR export steps (copy/paste for customers): 
1. Open Chrome DevTools -> Network.
2. Reproduce the request.
3. Right-click -> Save all as HAR with content.
4. Attach the HAR file to the ticket (or upload here).
Make sure they don't include private keys; we only need headers/body + response.

maria: Minimal curl we can ask for (replace placeholders):
```
curl -v 'https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED_API_KEY>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'X-Request-Ref: <if-present>' \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}'
```
Note: if their client strips the header, that shows up as no X-Request-Ref.

devon: SDK quick log tips: Node/Server SDK prints `request_ref` in the response object. Example: `const r = await client.generate(...); console.log('req', r.request_ref);`
Mobile RN/Android: ask them to enable console-level logging in the SDK and paste last ~20 lines around the failed request.

ryan: If there's no request_ref at all, check upstream proxies or CDN that might be stripping `X-Request-Ref` or `X-Forwarded-*`. Ask customer to include full request headers (we only need header names/values, redact auth). Also include any reverse-proxy config if known.

maria: For customers behind an edge proxy: please also send the proxy config or rules where headers might be rewritten. If possible, run the same curl from a machine outside the proxy (from laptop) to compare.

maria: If they provide a debug token, ask them to name it like `ticket-12345-<short>` so we can find it.

devon: If they attach a HAR, we need the exact network call entry (click the entry and copy timing/headers in devtools). If they can't attach a file, they can paste the Request/Response headers + body here.

maria: I'll paste a short checklist to send to the customer (one-liner):
- Timestamp (ISO) + region
- Minimal curl (headers + body) OR HAR file
- SDK logs (last 20 lines) or debug token from Console
- Any proxy/CDN config that touches request headers
- Redact api keys before sending

deploy-bot: debug-token-created debug-TKX-9Q2 (created by maria)

devon: Once we have the debug token/HAR/curl, I'll triage and try to reproduce. If I can't repro within 1 hour, I'll escalate to @ryan (eng) with the debug token + HAR + last 50 lines of server logs.

ryan: +1. If escalating, include product route, model name, and whether they used streaming. Streaming failures often have different traces.

maria: I'll send the checklist to the customer now and request the HAR + debug token. Will update here when they reply. If they send partial info (e.g., only screenshot), ask them to follow the checklist before we escalate.

maria: (follow-up note to self) If missing Request ID and customer is on our Dedicated plan, we can ask infra to pull tcpdump for the 1-second window — only after getting approval from account.
